# colab-remote-runner — Colab as a remote compute resource

Treat a Colab VM like a disposable remote box: create a session, push code and
data, run one or more batch commands, pull results back, stop it. Everything
goes through the official `colab` CLI (`uv tool install google-colab-cli`).
Verified with google-colab-cli 0.7.5 (2026-10) and 0.8.0 (2026-11); re-check
the gotchas after upgrading — the CLI is young and moves fast (`colab skill`
prints the CLI's own bundled agent notes).

## When to use / not

- ✅ Local GPU/RAM is busy or too small; want a T4/L4/A100 or a ~51 GB high-RAM
  shape for a few hours; want to run 2–3 configs in parallel off-box.
- ✅ The job is a **batch command** with a known input set and an output dir.
- ❌ Interactive exploration → Colab web UI. ❌ Queued / scheduled work across
  many jobs → `slurm-hpc`, `pueue-job-queue`. ❌ Data that may not leave your
  machine or must not sit in Google Drive.

## The shape of a run

```
local                                    Colab VM (/content/job)
uv build --wheel  ──colab upload──▶  wheels/ ── pip install (+ extras)
data in Drive     ─────────────────▶  Drive API download (Google network, fast)
                                      run CMD → OUT dir → tar
runs/ ◀──────────colab download────  result.tgz
colab stop (unless --keep)
```

`scripts/colab_job.py` implements all of it. Default flow:

```bash
# 1) One kept session per working block; Drive auth is interactive, once per session
colab new -s work --gpu T4 --high-mem
colab auth -s work            # browser sign-in, paste the code back (needed for Drive)

# 2) Plan first, then run any number of jobs on the same session
scripts/colab_job.py --dry-run run -s work --wheel . --data-spec data.json --cmd "..." --out runs/colab
scripts/colab_job.py run -s work --wheel . --pip catboost \
    --data-spec data.json --cmd "my-train --config cfg.yaml --out /content/job/out" \
    --tag config=cfg --out runs/colab
# later jobs on the same session: set "source": "present" in data.json (sha256 re-checked)

# 3) ALWAYS stop when done — idle sessions keep burning compute units
colab stop -s work            # `colab sessions` to see what is running
```

`run` creates the session if it does not exist and stops it at the end; an
existing session (or `--keep`) is left running. stdout is one JSON object;
everything else streams to stderr. Show the user its cost/time block:

| key | what |
|---|---|
| `timing_s` | wall seconds per phase: `session_new`, `upload`, `install`, `data`, `run`, `download`, `session_stop`, `total` |
| `cost.usage_before/during/after` | `colab usage` snapshots: `balance` (compute units), `rate_per_hr`, `active` |
| `cost.units_estimated` | `rate_per_hr` while assigned × this call's wall time |
| `cost.units_balance_delta` | balance before − after (can lag; trust the estimate for short runs) |
| `vm` | Python, CPUs, RAM, `nvidia-smi` GPUs on the VM |
| `result_dir` | local copy of the output dir; its `_colab_meta.json` holds all of the above + `cmd_seconds`, `peak_rss_gb`, tags |

`--export-log jsonl|md|ipynb` also saves `colab log` (the session's executed cells).

For a single self-contained script with no data or wheels, CLI ≥ 0.8's
`colab run [--gpu T4] script.py args…` (new + exec + stop in one call, also
usable as a shebang) is simpler than this script — but verify how it reports a
remote failure before scripting around its exit code.

## Decisions (defaults first)

| Question | Default | Why |
|---|---|---|
| How to ship code | `--wheel <project dir>` (local `uv build`) | No git token on the VM; exact local version; local path deps → pass each as its own `--wheel` |
| Where large data comes from | **Drive** (`"source": "drive"`) | Local upload is ~2 MB/s and chunked; Drive → VM is Google-internal and fast |
| When to `upload` data | `--smoke`-sized inputs (≤ ~1–2 GB) or no `colab auth` yet | ~10 min per GB-ish; fine for a smoke test only |
| Session lifetime | one named session + `--keep` for a block of runs | Amortizes boot, pip install, Drive auth and data download |
| Results | tar the output dir, `colab download`, log **locally** | Credentials for your tracker (MLflow etc.) never go to the VM |
| Provenance | tag runs `compute=colab`, GPU, high-mem | Colab package versions differ from local; you must be able to tell runs apart |

Data spec (`--data-spec data.json`; details in `references/drive-data.md`):

```json
{"source": "drive", "dest": "/content/data", "drive_folder": "datasets/my-dataset-v1",
 "files": [{"path": "features/2020.parquet", "sha256": "…"}, {"path": "labels.parquet", "sha256": "…"}]}
```

Only list the files **this** job needs (e.g. the years a config covers) —
fetching everything is the most common waste of time.

## Integrating into a project

Don't make the project depend on this script. Write a thin project wrapper that
derives the file list from the project's config, calls `colab_job.py run`
(or vendors its functions), then hands `result_dir` to the project's own
logger. Pattern + example in `references/adapting-to-a-project.md`.

## Gotchas

Each has symptom → cause → fix in `references/gotchas.md`.

- **`colab upload` → `400 Client Error: Bad Request`**: single request above
  ~60–94 MB is rejected, **and** the parent dir must already exist. Upload
  48 MiB chunks, mkdir first, reassemble + sha256 on the VM (`upload` does this).
- **`colab exec` exits 0 even when the remote code raised** (or called
  `sys.exit(3)`; re-checked on 0.8.0). Make every remote
  step print a marker (`__STEP_OK__ <step>`) and treat a missing marker as failure.
- **`colab exec --timeout` defaults to 30 s of silence**, not total runtime.
  pip / tar / a quiet `fit` trip it while the VM is still working. Pass a long
  timeout (script: 4 h) and treat "marker seen" as success even if the client
  then times out.
- **`colab drivemount` fails headless** (`ValueError: mount failed`). Use
  `colab auth -s S` (interactive, scope includes Drive) + the Drive API instead.
- **`RefreshError … metadata.google.internal … 404`** on the VM = no Google
  credentials yet; Colab VMs have no default service account. Run `colab auth`.
- **Auth can't be fully unattended.** `colab auth` needs a human in a browser
  once per session → that's why sessions are kept and reused.
- **CLI ≥ 0.8 keeps its OAuth token in the OS keyring.** Over SSH / headless the
  keyring is often locked: every `colab` call then waits 2 × 30 s, warns, and
  may re-prompt for sign-in. Unlock it, use `colab --auth=adc` (gcloud ADC with
  the scopes in `colab skill`), or pass `colab_job.py --no-keyring`
  (`PYTHON_KEYRING_BACKEND=keyring.backends.fail.Keyring`: falls back to the
  plaintext `~/.config/colab-cli/token.json` left from 0.7 — chmod it 600).
- **`colab auth` ≠ CLI auth.** `colab auth -s S` puts Google credentials *on the
  VM* (for Drive / GCS); a 401/403 from the CLI itself is a local credential or
  scope problem.
- **`RuntimeError: Connection was lost.`** mid-step: the kernel websocket
  dropped and the session may be gone server-side (`colab sessions` prunes it).
  Nothing to resume — rerun on a fresh session; keep steps idempotent.
- **Idle sessions bill.** `colab sessions`; `colab stop -s S`. Check
  `colab usage` for compute units.
- **Environment drift**: Colab ships its own Python (3.13 at time of writing),
  torch, xgboost, lightgbm; some libs (e.g. catboost) are absent → `--pip`.
  Expect tiny numeric differences vs local; CPU-deterministic paths can match
  bit-for-bit.
- **Credentials live only on the VM** and vanish on `colab stop`; nothing to
  clean up locally — but also nothing to reuse next session.
- **Speed calibration**: T4 is several × slower than a desktop RTX-class GPU;
  a full run that is mostly upload time is a sign you should move data to Drive.

## Validation loop

1. `--dry-run` → read the planned commands (session, uploads, steps, download, stop).
2. First real run with a smoke-sized config on a CPU/T4 session.
3. Confirm the result dir arrived and `_colab_meta.json` carries the tags.
4. `colab sessions` → nothing left running that you did not mean to keep.

## Reference files

- `scripts/colab_job.py` — `exec` / `upload` / `run`; `--help`, `--dry-run`, JSON stdout, exit 0/1/2.
- `assets/remote_steps.py` — the VM-side `install` / `data` / `run` steps (sent by `colab exec`).
- `assets/examples/` — verified smoke jobs: `fetch_datasette.py` (public Datasette table → CSV,
  429-aware), `lightgbm_smoke.py` (CPU), `keras_smoke.py` (GPU); commands in `references/smoke-test.md`.
- `references/gotchas.md` — symptom-titled traps with causes and fixes.
- `references/drive-data.md` — putting data on Drive, manifest format, Drive API fetch.
- `references/adapting-to-a-project.md` — thin project wrapper pattern.

## See also

- `long-running-jobs` — waiting for a multi-hour Colab run without polling in the model loop.
- `slurm-hpc`, `pueue-job-queue` — when the remote resource is a cluster or a local queue.
- `mlflow-tracking` — logging the downloaded run locally.

```text
from scipy.io.mmio import mmread
import os.path
import random # for sample selection

data_path = "Datasets/Epinions"
train_name = "EP25_UPL5_train.mtx"
test_name = "EP25_UPL5_test.mtx"

def load_epinions(path=data_path):
    # Scipy CSR: Compressed Sparce Row format
    train_data = mmread(os.path.join(path, train_name)).tocsr()
    test_data = mmread(os.path.join(path, test_name)).tocsr()
    return np.mean(MRR)

def main():
    TRAIN = True # Train or Load the model

    print("Loading Epinions dataset...")
    train_data, test_data = load_epinions()
    train_sample_users, test_sample_users = get_sample_users(train_data, test_data)

    print("Before training:")
    CF_model = CLiMF(train_data)
    print("aMRR of training data:", aMRRevaluate(train_data, CF_model, train_sample_users))
    print("aMRR of test data:", aMRRevaluate(test_data, CF_model, test_sample_users))

    if TRAIN:
        print("Training...")
        CF_model.train(verbose=True, sample_users=train_sample_users)
    else:
        print("Load pre-trained model...")
        CF_model.load()

    print("After training:")
    print("aMRR of training data:", aMRRevaluate(train_data, CF_model, train_sample_users))
    print("aMRR of test data:", aMRRevaluate(test_data, CF_model, test_sample_users))

    print("Result of U, V")
    print("U:", CF_model.U)
    print("V:", CF_model.V)

    CF_model.save() # save model

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Test sigmoid callable class
    # print(sigmoid(-87)())
    # print(sigmoid(87).derivative())
    main()


def _numpyToTorch(X, y=None):
    X_torch = torch.from_numpy(X).type(torch.FloatTensor)
    if y is not None:
        y_torch = torch.from_numpy(y).type(torch.FloatTensor).unsqueeze(1)
        return X_torch, y_torch
    return X_torch


def loadData(path):
    inputData = pd.read_csv(path)
    # Conventional features
    conventionalFeatures = inputData[[
        'Genre', 'Gross', 'Budget', 'Screens', 'Sequel', 'Ratings']]
    # Gross income is not available before release
    newFeatures = conventionalFeatures.drop(['Gross'], 1)
    # Deal with missing value
    newFeatures = newFeatures.dropna()

    y = np.array(newFeatures['Ratings'])  # y
    X = np.array(newFeatures.drop(['Ratings'], 1))  # X

    # Normalize or the loss/gradient will become nan/inf!!
    X = normalize(X)

    X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
        X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=87)
    return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test


def regression(X_train, y_train):
    learning_rate = 0.001
    X_train, y_train = _numpyToTorch(X_train, y_train)
    regression_model = torch.nn.Sequential(
        torch.nn.Linear(X_train.shape[1], 1))

    regression_model.train()

    optimizer = torch.optim.SGD(
        regression_model.parameters(), lr=learning_rate)

    t = trange(1000)
    for epoch in t:
        y_pred = regression_model(X_train)
        loss = torch.nn.functional.mse_loss(y_pred, y_train)
        t.set_postfix_str(f"epoch: {epoch+1}, loss: {loss.data.item()}")
        t.refresh()

        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
    # label_test = label[-5000:]

    return data_train, label_train, data_test, label_test
    
def trainSVM(data_train, label_train):
    clf = SVM(C=1, tol=0.001)
    clf.fit(data_train, label_train)
    return clf

def testAccuracy(data_test, label_test, clf):
    return clf.score(data_test, label_test)

def evaluateModel(data_test, label_test, clf):
    print(metrics.classification_report(label_test, clf.predict(data_test)))
    print(metrics.confusion_matrix(label_test, clf.predict(data_test)))

def main():
    # Load Data
    data_train, label_train, data_test, label_test = loadData('Datasets/MNIST.csv')

    # Train Model
    SVM_model = trainSVM(data_train, label_train)

    # Test Accuracy
    print('Accuracy:', float(testAccuracy(data_test, label_test, SVM_model)))

    # Evaluate Model
    evaluateModel(data_test, label_test, SVM_model)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

````text
# Adapting to a project: the thin-wrapper pattern

`colab_job.py` is project-agnostic. A project gets the best results with a
~100–200 line wrapper (e.g. `scripts/colab/run.py`) that knows three
project-specific things and delegates the rest.

## What the wrapper owns

1. **Which code to ship** — the project plus any local path dependencies
   (submodules, sibling packages) as wheels. Ship config files too (tar the
   `configs/` dir and `--upload` it), because wheels usually don't include them.
2. **Which data a job needs** — derive the file list from the job config
   (e.g. the years/segments it trains and tests on) and the project's data
   manifest; write the data spec JSON.
3. **What to do with results** — the remote command writes to a fixed output
   root with tracking disabled (`--no-tracking`-style flag); after download the
   wrapper calls the project's own "log this run dir" command locally, so
   tracker credentials never leave the machine.

## Sketch

```python
spec = {
    "source": args.data,
    "dest": "/content/data",
    "drive_folder": DRIVE_FOLDER,
    "files": needed_files(cfg),
}  # project logic
Path(tmp, "data.json").write_text(json.dumps(spec))
cmd = f"DATA_DIR=/content/data my-run {args.config} --no-tracking --runs-root /content/job/out"
subprocess.run(
    [
        COLAB_JOB,
        "run",
        "-s",
        session,
        "--wheel",
        ".",
        "--wheel",
        "libs/dep",
        "--upload",
        "configs:/content/job/configs",
        "--data-spec",
        f"{tmp}/data.json",
        "--cmd",
        cmd,
        "--tag",
        f"config={args.config}",
        "--out",
        "runs/colab",
        *(["--keep"] if args.keep else []),
    ],
    check=True,
    stdout=PIPE,
)
result = json.loads(proc.stdout)
log_run_dirs(Path(result["result_dir"]).iterdir())  # project logger, locally
```

## Choices that paid off

- **Model-specific extras** map (`{"CatBoost...": ["catboost>=1.2"]}`) — install
  only what this config needs on top of Colab's preinstalled stack.
- **Memory-lean modes** (streaming / external-memory training) let a standard
  ~12.7 GB VM run what otherwise needs the ~51 GB high-RAM shape.
- **A persistent session for a sweep**: first job uses `source: drive`, later
  ones `source: present`.
- **Record a measured comparison** (local vs Colab: wall time split into boot /
  install / data / fit / download, peak RSS, metric deltas) in the project's
  docs, so the next person knows whether Colab is worth it for their job.
- Expose the same thing as a backend in any job launcher you have
  (pueue / Slurm / Colab behind one `submit` interface).
````

```markdown
# 讓 Algorithm/ 每個實驗都能在 Colab 跑起來 + compute unit 估算

## Context 背景

想把 repo 裡的實驗丟到 Colab（透過 `colab-remote-runner` skill 的 `colab_job.py`）當遠端算力，
並知道每個實驗該用哪種 runtime、要花多少 compute unit（CU）。

盤點結果（已確認）：
- `Algorithm/` 下約 30 個可執行 `.py`，全部是小型 CPU 工作；資料都在 `Datasets/`（共約 130 MB，最大 `MNIST.csv` 77 MB），腳本以 **repo root 為 cwd** 讀 `Datasets/...`。
- **沒有任何實驗真正需要 GPU**（唯一的 torch 腳本 `LinearRegression_CSM_pytorch.py` 是 CPU、1000 epoch 的小線性模型）。
- Colab = Python 3.13 + pandas 2 / 新版 sklearn → 目前多數腳本會壞：
  - 14 處 `df.drop([...], 1)`（pandas 2 移除 positional axis）
  - `Boosting_..._LightGBM.py`: `sklearn.cross_validation`
  - `SVM_Iris_Multiclass.py`: `sys.path.append("../SVM_MNIST")` 依賴 cwd + 需要 `mlxtend`
  - 可能還有 sklearn 參數移除（如 AdaBoost `algorithm='SAMME.R'`、LogisticRegression `multi_class`）— 在本機相容性測試中逐一發現
  - `plt.show()` headless → 設 `MPLBACKEND=Agg`
- 本機 `colab` CLI 可用，帳戶餘額 **571.15 CU**，目前無 active session。Keyring 鎖住 → 一律用 `colab_job.py --no-keyring`（或 `colab --auth=adc`）。
- 決策（使用者已選）：**直接修原始碼**；範圍 **只做 `Algorithm/`**，`Project/KaggleElo`、`Project/DCIC2019`、`CLiMF_Epinions_TensorFlow.py`（TF1 `contrib`）列為 follow-up，只在 manifest 標記需求與估算。

## Runtime 建議與 CU 估算

費率為 Colab 公開的近似值（會隨方案變動），Phase 3 smoke 時用 `colab usage` 的 `rate_per_hr` 實測並回填。

| Tier | 實驗 | 建議 runtime | 預估 Colab 時間 | 近似費率 | 預估 CU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A 秒級 | sklearn 版全部、LinearRegression×3、LogisticRegression×2、NaiveBayes×2、PCA×2、Post-Operative×2、AdaBoost/Adaboost×4、LightGBM、SVM_Iris | CPU 標準 | 每個 < 1 min，合計 ~5 min | ~0.07–0.1 CU/h | < 0.02 |
| B 分鐘級 (純 Python 迴圈) | kNN_FromScratch、DecisionTree_FromScratch、KMeans×2、FP-Growth(retail)、SVD_MSWeb、VSM/LSI Gensim、SVM_MNIST_Binary | CPU 標準 | 合計 ~20–40 min | 同上 | ~0.05 |
| C 可能較久 | SVM_MNIST_Multiclass_FromScratch（10× SMO）、CLiMF_FromScratch | CPU 標準（VSM 若 RAM 吃緊改 `--high-mem`） | 各 10–60 min | 同上 / high-mem ~0.13 CU/h | ~0.1 |
| D 選配 | HMM `CompareJiebaHanLP.py`（`pyhanlp` 需 JVM + 首次下載資料） | CPU | ~5 min | — | ~0.01 |
| Follow-up | KaggleElo（~3 GB CSV） | CPU `--high-mem`（~51 GB） | 1–2 h | ~0.13 CU/h | ~0.3 |
| Follow-up | DCIC2019（xgboost K-fold） | CPU 或 T4 | < 1 h | CPU ~0.1 / T4 ~1.5–1.8 CU/h | 0.1 / ~2 |

**結論**：全部 Algorithm 實驗在單一 CPU session 跑完 ≈ 1–1.5 h，**< 0.5 CU**；就算全改 T4 也只 ~2–3 CU。GPU 對這些實驗沒有加速效果，不建議開。

## Plan 實作步驟

### Phase 1 — 相容性修正（本機，不花 CU）
1. 用接近 Colab 的環境逐一跑腳本找錯：
   `uv run --python 3.13 --with pandas,numpy,scikit-learn,scipy,matplotlib,lightgbm,torch,tqdm,gensim,cvxopt,mlxtend python <script>`（cwd = repo root，`MPLBACKEND=Agg`，每個加 `timeout`）。
2. 最小修改原始碼：
   - `drop([...], 1)` → `drop(columns=[...])`（DecisionTree×2、KMeans×2、LinearRegression×3、NaiveBayes、SVM_MNIST×2、kNN×2）
```

```text
## Approved Plan:
# 讓 Algorithm/ 每個實驗都能在 Colab 跑起來 + compute unit 估算

## Context 背景

想把 repo 裡的實驗丟到 Colab（透過 `colab-remote-runner` skill 的 `colab_job.py`）當遠端算力，
並知道每個實驗該用哪種 runtime、要花多少 compute unit（CU）。

盤點結果（已確認）：
- `Algorithm/` 下約 30 個可執行 `.py`，全部是小型 CPU 工作；資料都在 `Datasets/`（共約 130 MB，最大 `MNIST.csv` 77 MB），腳本以 **repo root 為 cwd** 讀 `Datasets/...`。
- **沒有任何實驗真正需要 GPU**（唯一的 torch 腳本 `LinearRegression_CSM_pytorch.py` 是 CPU、1000 epoch 的小線性模型）。
- Colab = Python 3.13 + pandas 2 / 新版 sklearn → 目前多數腳本會壞：
  - 14 處 `df.drop([...], 1)`（pandas 2 移除 positional axis）
  - `Boosting_..._LightGBM.py`: `sklearn.cross_validation`
  - `SVM_Iris_Multiclass.py`: `sys.path.append("../SVM_MNIST")` 依賴 cwd + 需要 `mlxtend`
  - 可能還有 sklearn 參數移除（如 AdaBoost `algorithm='SAMME.R'`、LogisticRegression `multi_class`）— 在本機相容性測試中逐一發現
  - `plt.show()` headless → 設 `MPLBACKEND=Agg`
- 本機 `colab` CLI 可用，帳戶餘額 **571.15 CU**，目前無 active session。Keyring 鎖住 → 一律用 `colab_job.py --no-keyring`（或 `colab --auth=adc`）。
- 決策（使用者已選）：**直接修原始碼**；範圍 **只做 `Algorithm/`**，`Project/KaggleElo`、`Project/DCIC2019`、`CLiMF_Epinions_TensorFlow.py`（TF1 `contrib`）列為 follow-up，只在 manifest 標記需求與估算。

## Runtime 建議與 CU 估算

費率為 Colab 公開的近似值（會隨方案變動），Phase 3 smoke 時用 `colab usage` 的 `rate_per_hr` 實測並回填。

| Tier | 實驗 | 建議 runtime | 預估 Colab 時間 | 近似費率 | 預估 CU |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A 秒級 | sklearn 版全部、LinearRegression×3、LogisticRegression×2、NaiveBayes×2、PCA×2、Post-Operative×2、AdaBoost/Adaboost×4、LightGBM、SVM_Iris | CPU 標準 | 每個 < 1 min，合計 ~5 min | ~0.07–0.1 CU/h | < 0.02 |
| B 分鐘級 (純 Python 迴圈) | kNN_FromScratch、DecisionTree_FromScratch、KMeans×2、FP-Growth(retail)、SVD_MSWeb、VSM/LSI Gensim、SVM_MNIST_Binary | CPU 標準 | 合計 ~20–40 min | 同上 | ~0.05 |
| C 可能較久 | SVM_MNIST_Multiclass_FromScratch（10× SMO）、CLiMF_FromScratch | CPU 標準（VSM 若 RAM 吃緊改 `--high-mem`） | 各 10–60 min | 同上 / high-mem ~0.13 CU/h | ~0.1 |
| D 選配 | HMM `CompareJiebaHanLP.py`（`pyhanlp` 需 JVM + 首次下載資料） | CPU | ~5 min | — | ~0.01 |
| Follow-up | KaggleElo（~3 GB CSV） | CPU `--high-mem`（~51 GB） | 1–2 h | ~0.13 CU/h | ~0.3 |
| Follow-up | DCIC2019（xgboost K-fold） | CPU 或 T4 | < 1 h | CPU ~0.1 / T4 ~1.5–1.8 CU/h | 0.1 / ~2 |

**結論**：全部 Algorithm 實驗在單一 CPU session 跑完 ≈ 1–1.5 h，**< 0.5 CU**；就算全改 T4 也只 ~2–3 CU。GPU 對這些實驗沒有加速效果，不建議開。
```

```text
class LinearRegression:

    # Calculate weights
    def __calcWeights(self, xArr, yArr):
        xData = np.asmatrix(xArr)
        xMat = np.hstack([np.ones((len(xArr), 1)), xData]) # Append a constant 1 column in the first column
        yMat = np.asmatrix(yArr).T
        xTx = xMat.T * xMat
        if np.linalg.det(xTx) == 0:
            # TODO: Should use gradient descent!
            # can refer to https://github.com/mlelarge/dataflowr/blob/master/Notebooks/02_basics_pytorch.ipynb
            print("This matrix is singular, cannot do inverse")
            return
        ws = xTx.I * (xMat.T * yMat)
        return ws

    def rssError(self, yArr, yHatArr):
        return ((yArr - yHatArr)**2).sum()

    def fit(self, X, y):
        self.weights = self.__calcWeights(X, y)

    def __predictOne(self, x):
        yHat = np.asmatrix(x) * self.weights
        return yHat

    def predict(self, X_test):
        m = np.shape(X_test)[0]
        if m == 1:
            return self.__predictOne(np.hstack([1, X_test])) # Append a constant 1 in from of the row
        else:
            prediction = np.zeros(m)
            xMat = np.hstack([np.ones((len(X_test), 1)), X_test]) # Append a constant 1 column in the first column
            for i, rowVector in enumerate(xMat):
                prediction[i] = self.__predictOne(rowVector)
            return prediction
    
    ## Score method
    # Method diff: the difference of y true and y predicted is less than diff
    # Method R2: the coefficient of determination R^2 of the prediction (Best is 0)
```

```text
def cmd_run(a: argparse.Namespace, result: dict) -> dict:
    """Fills `result` in place so timing/cost survive a failed step."""
    spec = json.loads(Path(a.data_spec).read_text()) if a.data_spec else None
    if spec and spec.get("source") not in {"drive", "upload", "present"}:
        raise SystemExit("data-spec.source must be drive | upload | present")
    ph = Phases()
    usage_before = usage_snapshot()
    usage_during: dict = {}
    reused = session_exists(a.session)
    if not reused:
        new = ["new", "-s", a.session]
        if a.gpu.lower() != "none":
            new += ["--gpu", a.gpu]
        if a.high_mem:
            new.append("--high-mem")
        with ph("session_new"):
            colab(*new)
    stop = not (a.keep or reused)
    result |= {"session": a.session, "reused": reused}
    try:
        usage_during = usage_snapshot()  # burn rate while this VM is assigned
        # 1) code: wheels built locally (no git credentials needed on the VM)
        with ph("upload"):
            remote_mkdir(a.session, [f"{WORK}/wheels", a.collect])
            if a.wheel:
                dist = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="colab-dist-"))
                for proj in a.wheel:
                    cmd = ["uv", "build", "--wheel", "-q", "-o", str(dist), proj]
                    PLAN.append(" ".join(cmd))
                    log("+", " ".join(cmd))
                    if not DRY:
                        subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, stdout=sys.stderr)
                wheels = sorted(dist.glob("*.whl"))
                upload_files(
                    a.session, [(w, f"{WORK}/wheels/{w.name}") for w in wheels]
                )
                shutil.rmtree(dist, ignore_errors=True)
            for item in a.upload:
                local, _, remote = item.partition(":")
                if not remote:
                    raise SystemExit(f"--upload must be LOCAL:REMOTE, got {item!r}")
                upload_path(a.session, Path(local), remote)
        if a.wheel or a.pip:
            with ph("install"):
                remote_step(
                    a.session,
                    {"step": "install", "wheel_dir": f"{WORK}/wheels", "pip": a.pip},
                )
        # 2) data
        if spec:
            with ph("data"):
                dest = spec.get("dest", "/content/data")
                if spec["source"] == "upload":
                    local_dir = Path(spec["local_dir"])
                    pairs = [
                        (local_dir / f["path"], f"{dest}/{f['path']}")
                        for f in spec["files"]
                    ]
                    upload_files(a.session, pairs)
                remote_step(a.session, {
                    "step": "data", "dest": dest, "files": spec["files"],
                    "source": "drive" if spec["source"] == "drive" else "present",
                    "drive_folder": spec.get("drive_folder", ""),
                })  # fmt: skip
        # 3) command, then collect
        tags = {
            "compute": "colab",
            "colab_gpu": a.gpu,
            "colab_high_mem": str(a.high_mem),
            **kv(a.tag, "--tag"),
        }
        archive = f"{WORK}/result.tgz"
        with ph("run"):
            remote_step(a.session, {
                "step": "run", "cmd": a.cmd, "cwd": WORK, "env": kv(a.env, "--env"),
                "collect": a.collect, "archive": archive, "tags": tags,
            })  # fmt: skip
        out = Path(a.out)
        out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        local_tgz = out / f"{a.session}-{int(time.time())}.tgz"
        with ph("download"):
            colab("download", "-s", a.session, archive, str(local_tgz))
            if not DRY:
                with tarfile.open(local_tgz) as tar:
                    try:
                        tar.extractall(out, filter="data")
                    except TypeError:  # Python without tarfile filters
                        tar.extractall(out)
                local_tgz.unlink()
        result |= {"result_dir": str(out / Path(a.collect).name), "tags": tags}
        if a.export_log:
            log_path = out / f"{a.session}-log.{a.export_log}"
            colab("log", "-s", a.session, "-o", str(log_path))
            result["session_log"] = str(log_path)
    finally:
        if stop:
            with ph("session_stop"):
                colab("stop", "-s", a.session)
        result["stopped"] = stop
        seconds = ph.total()
        # The VM keeps billing while kept, so "units" covers only this call's wall time.
        result["timing_s"] = {**ph.secs, "total": seconds}
        result["cost"] = cost_summary(
            usage_before, usage_during, usage_snapshot(), seconds
        )
        meta_path = Path(result.get("result_dir", "")) / "_colab_meta.json"
        if not DRY and meta_path.is_file():
            meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())
            meta |= {
                "timing_s": result["timing_s"],
                "cost": result["cost"],
                "session": a.session,
            }
            meta_path.write_text(json.dumps(meta, indent=2))
            result["vm"] = meta.get("vm", {})
    return result


def main() -> int:
    global DRY
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(

    ap.add_argument(

    u = sub.add_parser("upload", help="chunked upload of a file or directory")
    u.add_argument("--session", "-s", required=True)
    u.add_argument("local")
```

```text
def step_run(p: dict) -> None:
    env = {**os.environ, **p.get("env", {})}
    collect = Path(p["collect"])
    collect.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    print("+", p["cmd"], flush=True)
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        p["cmd"], shell=True, cwd=p["cwd"], env=env,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True,
    )  # fmt: skip
    for line in proc.stdout:  # stream: a quiet step is what trips client timeouts
        print(line, end="", flush=True)
    if proc.wait() != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"command exited {proc.returncode}")
    meta = {
        "tags": p.get("tags", {}),
        "vm": vm_info(),
        "cmd": p["cmd"],
        "cmd_seconds": round(time.monotonic() - t0, 1),
        # ru_maxrss is KiB on Linux: the largest single descendant process, not the sum
        "peak_rss_gb": round(
            resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss / 1024**2, 2
        ),
    }
    (collect / "_colab_meta.json").write_text(json.dumps(meta, indent=2))
    with tarfile.open(p["archive"], "w:gz") as tar:
        tar.add(collect, arcname=collect.name)
    print(json.dumps({"collected": str(collect), "archive": p["archive"]}))
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run selected experiments from experiments.toml, one after another (VM side).

Runs from the repo root (scripts read `Datasets/...` relative to it). For each
experiment: stream its output, save it to OUT/logs/<name>.log, save any
matplotlib figures to OUT/figures/<name>/, and record exit code, wall seconds
and peak RSS in OUT/summary.json.

Always exits 0 once the summary is written: colab_job.py only downloads the
output dir when the remote command succeeds, and a failed experiment must not
hide the results of the others. Read `summary.json` for per-experiment status.

usage: vm_run_all.py --out DIR NAME [NAME ...]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
SITE = HERE / "_site"  # sitecustomize.py: plt.show() -> savefig


def load_manifest() -> dict[str, dict]:
    raw = tomllib.loads((HERE / "experiments.toml").read_text())
    defaults = raw.get("defaults", {})
    return {e["name"]: {**defaults, **e} for e in raw["experiment"]}


def run_one(exp: dict, out: Path) -> dict:
    name = exp["name"]
    log_path = out / "logs" / f"{name}.log"
    fig_dir = out / "figures" / name
    log_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    env = {
        **os.environ,
        "MPLBACKEND": "Agg",
        "PYTHONUNBUFFERED": "1",
        "COLAB_FIG_DIR": str(fig_dir),
        "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join(
            p for p in (str(SITE), os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH", "")) if p
        ),
    }
    timeout_s = int(float(exp["timeout_min"]) * 60)
    print(f"\n===== {name} ({exp['script']}, timeout {timeout_s}s) =====", flush=True)
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        [sys.executable, exp["script"]],
        cwd=ROOT,
        env=env,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
        errors="replace",
    )
    timed_out = threading.Event()

    def kill() -> None:
        timed_out.set()
        proc.kill()

    timer = threading.Timer(timeout_s, kill)
    timer.start()
    with log_path.open("w") as log:
        for line in proc.stdout:  # keep streaming: silence trips the client timeout
            log.write(line)
            print(f"[{name}] {line}", end="", flush=True)
    _, status, rusage = os.wait4(proc.pid, 0)
    timer.cancel()
    rc = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status)
    proc.returncode = rc
    secs = round(time.monotonic() - t0, 1)
    rec = {
        "name": name,
        "script": exp["script"],
        "tier": exp.get("tier"),
        "rc": rc,
        "ok": rc == 0 and not timed_out.is_set(),
        "timed_out": timed_out.is_set(),
        "seconds": secs,
        "peak_rss_gb": round(rusage.ru_maxrss / 1024**2, 3),  # KiB on Linux
        "figures": sorted(p.name for p in fig_dir.glob("*.png")),
    }
    print(f"===== {name}: rc={rc} {secs}s ok={rec['ok']} =====", flush=True)
    return rec


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("names", nargs="+")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    manifest = load_manifest()
    unknown = [n for n in a.names if n not in manifest]
    if unknown:
        print(f"unknown experiments: {unknown}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    a.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    results = []
    for n in a.names:
        results.append(run_one(manifest[n], a.out))
        # rewrite after every experiment so a lost connection still leaves partial results
        (a.out / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    failed = [r["name"] for r in results if not r["ok"]]
    print(f"\n{len(results) - len(failed)}/{len(results)} ok; failed: {failed}", flush=True)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

```python
"""Loaded automatically via PYTHONPATH by vm_run_all.py.

Headless runs have no display, so turn `plt.show()` into "save every open
figure to $COLAB_FIG_DIR" instead of silently dropping the plots.
"""

import os

_fig_dir = os.environ.get("COLAB_FIG_DIR")

if _fig_dir:
    try:
        import matplotlib

        matplotlib.use("Agg")
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

        _count = [0]

        def _save_and_close(*_args, **_kwargs):
            os.makedirs(_fig_dir, exist_ok=True)
            for num in plt.get_fignums():
                _count[0] += 1
                plt.figure(num).savefig(os.path.join(_fig_dir, f"fig{_count[0]:02d}.png"), dpi=110, bbox_inches="tight")
            plt.close("all")

        plt.show = _save_and_close
    except ImportError:  # matplotlib not installed: nothing to patch
        pass
```

```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = []
# ///
"""Run Algorithm/ experiments on a Google Colab VM, or estimate their cost.

Thin project wrapper around the colab-remote-runner skill's colab_job.py:
it picks experiments from tools/colab/experiments.toml, ships the scripts plus
only the Datasets/ files they read as one tarball, runs them sequentially in a
single Colab session (tools/colab/vm_run_all.py), downloads logs/figures/summary
and writes a report with per-experiment time and compute-unit share.

Examples
  tools/colab/run_experiments.py --estimate                     # table, no Colab call
  tools/colab/run_experiments.py --tier A --dry-run             # planned colab commands
  tools/colab/run_experiments.py --tier A                       # smoke run on a CPU VM
  tools/colab/run_experiments.py --tier A,B,C --rate 0.07       # everything that is ready
  tools/colab/run_experiments.py --only svm-mnist-binary-scratch --keep -s work

stdout: one JSON object (result + report path, or the estimate / plan).
stderr: progress and remote output. Exit codes: 0 ok (see report for failed
experiments), 1 Colab / CLI failure, 2 usage error.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
import tempfile
import time
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = HERE.parent.parent
COLAB_JOB = ROOT / ".claude/skills/colab-remote-runner/scripts/colab_job.py"
REMOTE_TGZ = "/content/job/repo.tgz"
REMOTE_OUT = "/content/job/out"

# Approximate Colab compute-unit burn rates (units/hour). They depend on the
# plan and change over time: the real rate is measured during a run
# (`cost.usage_during.rate_per_hr`) - pass it back with --rate.
APPROX_RATE = {
    "cpu": 0.08,
    "cpu-highmem": 0.13,
    "T4": 1.8,
    "L4": 4.8,
    "A100": 12.0,
    "H100": 18.0,
}
# Per-session overhead: VM boot + upload + pip install + download + stop.
OVERHEAD_MIN = 4.0
RUNTIME_FLAGS = {  # runtime -> (colab_job --gpu, --high-mem)
    "cpu": ("none", False),
    "cpu-highmem": ("none", True),
    "T4": ("T4", False),
    "L4": ("L4", False),
    "A100": ("A100", False),
    "H100": ("H100", False),
}


def log(*a: object) -> None:
    print(*a, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


def load_manifest() -> list[dict]:
    raw = tomllib.loads((HERE / "experiments.toml").read_text())
    defaults = raw.get("defaults", {})
    return [{"pip": [], "data": [], **defaults, **e} for e in raw["experiment"]]


def select(exps: list[dict], a: argparse.Namespace) -> list[dict]:
    if a.only:
        names = {n.strip() for n in a.only.split(",")}
        unknown = names - {e["name"] for e in exps}
        if unknown:
            raise SystemExit(f"unknown experiments: {sorted(unknown)}")
        return [e for e in exps if e["name"] in names]
    tiers = {t.strip().upper() for t in a.tier.split(",")} if a.tier else None
    status = {s.strip() for s in a.status.split(",")}
    return [
        e
        for e in exps
        if e["status"] in status and (tiers is None or e["tier"] in tiers)
    ]


def estimate(sel: list[dict], a: argparse.Namespace) -> dict:
    rows, by_runtime = [], {}
    for e in sel:
        rt = a.runtime or e["runtime"]
        rate = a.rate if a.rate is not None else APPROX_RATE[rt]
        units = e["est_min"] / 60 * rate
        rows.append({"name": e["name"], "tier": e["tier"], "status": e["status"],
                     "runtime": rt, "est_min": e["est_min"], "units": round(units, 4),
                     "note": e.get("note", "")})  # fmt: skip
        g = by_runtime.setdefault(rt, {"experiments": 0, "est_min": 0.0, "rate_per_hr": rate})
        g["experiments"] += 1
        g["est_min"] += e["est_min"]
    for g in by_runtime.values():  # one session per runtime shape
        g["session_min"] = round(g["est_min"] + OVERHEAD_MIN, 1)
        g["units"] = round(g["session_min"] / 60 * g["rate_per_hr"], 3)
    total = round(sum(g["units"] for g in by_runtime.values()), 3)
    # human table on stderr
    log(f"{'experiment':34} {'tier':4} {'status':8} {'runtime':11} {'min':>6} {'CU':>7}")
    for r in rows:
        log(f"{r['name']:34} {r['tier']:4} {r['status']:8} {r['runtime']:11} {r['est_min']:6.1f} {r['units']:7.3f}")
    for rt, g in by_runtime.items():
        log(f"session {rt:11}: {g['experiments']} experiments, ~{g['session_min']} min incl. "
            f"{OVERHEAD_MIN} min overhead, {g['rate_per_hr']} CU/h -> ~{g['units']} CU")  # fmt: skip
    log(f"total ~{total} CU (rates are approximate unless --rate was given)")
    return {"estimate": rows, "sessions": by_runtime, "total_units": total}


def build_tarball(sel: list[dict], dest: Path) -> tuple[Path, int]:
    files = {Path("pyproject.toml")}
    files |= {p.relative_to(ROOT) for p in (ROOT / "Algorithm").rglob("*.py")}
    files |= {p.relative_to(ROOT) for p in HERE.rglob("*.py")}
    files.add(Path("tools/colab/experiments.toml"))
    for e in sel:
        files |= {Path(d) for d in e["data"]}
    missing = [str(f) for f in files if not (ROOT / f).is_file()]
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit(f"missing files: {missing}")
    tgz = dest / "repo.tgz"
    with tarfile.open(tgz, "w:gz") as tar:
        for f in sorted(files):
            if "__pycache__" not in f.parts:
                tar.add(ROOT / f, arcname=str(f))
    return tgz, len(files)


def write_report(run_dir: Path, result: dict, rate_hint: float) -> Path:
    summary_path = run_dir / "summary.json"
    summary = json.loads(summary_path.read_text()) if summary_path.is_file() else []
    cost = result.get("cost", {})
    timing = result.get("timing_s", {})
    units = cost.get("units_estimated")
    rate = (cost.get("usage_during") or {}).get("rate_per_hr") or rate_hint
    run_s = sum(r["seconds"] for r in summary) or 1.0
    lines = [
        f"# Colab run {run_dir.name}",
        "",
        f"- session: `{result.get('session')}`  VM: {json.dumps(result.get('vm', {}))}",
        f"- measured rate: {rate} CU/h; this call ~{units} CU "
        f"(balance delta {cost.get('units_balance_delta')})",
        "- phases (s): " + ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in timing.items()),
        "",
        "| experiment | tier | ok | rc | seconds | peak RSS GB | figures | CU share |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for r in summary:
        share = round(units * r["seconds"] / run_s, 4) if units else "-"
        ok = "yes" if r["ok"] else ("TIMEOUT" if r["timed_out"] else "NO")
        lines.append(f"| {r['name']} | {r['tier']} | {ok} | {r['rc']} | {r['seconds']} | "
                     f"{r['peak_rss_gb']} | {len(r['figures'])} | {share} |")  # fmt: skip
    n_ok = sum(r["ok"] for r in summary)
    lines += ["", f"{n_ok}/{len(summary)} ok. Logs: `logs/<name>.log`, figures: `figures/<name>/`."]
    report = run_dir / "report.md"
    report.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    return report


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--only", help="comma-separated experiment names")
    ap.add_argument("--tier", help="comma-separated tiers, e.g. A,B,C (default: all)")
    ap.add_argument("--status", default="ready", help="comma-separated: ready,optional,followup")
    ap.add_argument("--runtime", choices=sorted(RUNTIME_FLAGS), help="override the manifest runtime")
    ap.add_argument("--rate", type=float, help="CU/hour to use for --estimate (measured value)")
    ap.add_argument("--estimate", action="store_true", help="print time/CU estimate only")
    ap.add_argument("--session", "-s", default="ml-practice")
    ap.add_argument("--keep", action="store_true", help="leave the session running")
    ap.add_argument("--use-keyring", action="store_true",
                    help="let the colab CLI use the OS keyring (default: --no-keyring)")  # fmt: skip
    ap.add_argument("--out", default="runs/colab", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    sel = select(load_manifest(), a)
    if not sel:
        log("no experiments selected")
        return 2
    if a.estimate:
        print(json.dumps(estimate(sel, a), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        return 0
    not_ready = [e["name"] for e in sel if e["status"] == "followup"]
    if not_ready:
        log(f"refusing to run follow-up experiments (see their `note`): {not_ready}")
        return 2
    runtimes = {a.runtime or e["runtime"] for e in sel}
    if len(runtimes) > 1:
        log(f"selection mixes runtimes {sorted(runtimes)}; run them separately or pass --runtime")
        return 2
    runtime = runtimes.pop()
    gpu, high_mem = RUNTIME_FLAGS[runtime]
    pip = sorted({p for e in sel for p in e["pip"]})
    names = [e["name"] for e in sel]
    run_dir = (ROOT / a.out / time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")).resolve()

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="colab-ml-") as tmp:
        tgz, n_files = build_tarball(sel, Path(tmp))
        log(f"tarball: {n_files} files, {tgz.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB; "
            f"{len(names)} experiments on {runtime}; pip: {pip or '-'}")  # fmt: skip
        remote = (
            f"mkdir -p repo && tar xzf {REMOTE_TGZ} -C repo && cd repo && "
            f"python tools/colab/vm_run_all.py --out {REMOTE_OUT} {' '.join(names)}"
        )
        cmd = [sys.executable, str(COLAB_JOB)]
        cmd += ["--dry-run"] if a.dry_run else []
        cmd += [] if a.use_keyring else ["--no-keyring"]
        cmd += ["run", "-s", a.session, "--gpu", gpu, "--upload", f"{tgz}:{REMOTE_TGZ}",
                "--cmd", remote, "--collect", REMOTE_OUT, "--out", str(run_dir),
                "--tag", f"runtime={runtime}", "--tag", f"experiments={','.join(names)}"]  # fmt: skip
        cmd += ["--high-mem"] if high_mem else []
        cmd += ["--keep"] if a.keep else []
        for p in pip:
            cmd += ["--pip", p]
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)

    try:
        result = json.loads(proc.stdout)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        log(proc.stdout)
        log(f"colab_job.py exited {proc.returncode} without JSON output")
        return 1
    if a.dry_run:
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
        return proc.returncode
    out_dir = Path(result.get("result_dir", run_dir / "out"))
    if out_dir.is_dir():
        result["report"] = str(write_report(out_dir, result, APPROX_RATE[runtime]))
        log(Path(result["report"]).read_text())
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 0 if proc.returncode == 0 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

````markdown
# Running the experiments on Google Colab

`tools/colab/` runs the scripts under `Algorithm/` on a Colab VM through the
official `colab` CLI, using the `colab-remote-runner` skill's
`.claude/skills/colab-remote-runner/scripts/colab_job.py` for the session /
upload / exec / download / stop plumbing.

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `experiments.toml` | manifest: script, data files, extra pip packages, tier, recommended runtime, timeout, estimated minutes, status |
| `run_experiments.py` | local entry point: select experiments, `--estimate`, or ship + run + download + `report.md` |
| `vm_run_all.py` | VM side: run the selected experiments one by one, per-experiment logs / figures / `summary.json` |
| `_site/sitecustomize.py` | on the VM, `plt.show()` saves figures to `figures/<name>/` instead of dropping them |

## Quick start

```bash
uv tool install google-colab-cli        # once; any colab command triggers the OAuth sign-in
tools/colab/run_experiments.py --estimate              # time / compute-unit table, no Colab call
tools/colab/run_experiments.py --tier A --dry-run      # planned colab commands
tools/colab/run_experiments.py --tier A,B              # run every ready experiment on one CPU VM
tools/colab/run_experiments.py --only svm-mnist-binary-scratch
colab sessions                                         # make sure nothing is left running
```

Results land in `runs/colab/<timestamp>/out/` (git-ignored): `report.md`,
`summary.json`, `logs/<name>.log`, `figures/<name>/*.png`, `_colab_meta.json`.

The CLI stores its OAuth token in the OS keyring; when the keyring is locked
(SSH / headless) every call waits 2 x 30 s. The wrapper therefore passes
`--no-keyring` by default (falls back to `~/.config/colab-cli/token.json`);
use `--use-keyring` to opt out.

## Runtime choice and cost

None of the experiments benefits from a GPU: they are small scikit-learn / NumPy
/ pure-Python workloads, and the only PyTorch script trains a single linear
layer on a few hundred rows. A standard CPU VM is the right shape for all of
them; GPU runtimes burn compute units 20-100x faster for no speed-up.

| tier | experiments | runtime | local wall time (Python 3.13) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 23 sklearn / from-scratch scripts (AdaBoost, LightGBM, KMeans, LinearRegression x3 incl. PyTorch, LogisticRegression, NaiveBayes, PCA, SVD, VSM/LSI gensim, SVM Iris / Post-Operative, kNN) | cpu | < 6 s each |
| B | DecisionTree from scratch, FP-Growth (retail), SVM MNIST binary / multiclass, CLiMF from scratch | cpu | 18 s - 2.7 min each |
| D (optional) | HMM jieba vs. HanLP | cpu | needs a JDK + ~600 MB HanLP data download |

COLAB_MEASURED_PLACEHOLDER

## Follow-ups (not runnable yet)

| experiment | blocker | suggested runtime |
|---|---|---|
| `Algorithm/CLiMF/CLiMF_Epinions/CLiMF_Epinions_TensorFlow.py` | `tensorflow.contrib.eager` (TF1) - needs a TF2 rewrite | cpu is enough (T4 only if the model grows) |
| `Project/KaggleElo` | ~3 GB Kaggle data (put it on Drive, use a data spec) and > 12.7 GB pandas peak RAM | `cpu-highmem` (~51 GB) |
| `Project/DCIC2019` | competition data not in the repo; `sklearn.externals.joblib` removed; expects feature pickles | cpu |

## Compatibility fixes applied to the scripts

To run on a current stack (Colab ships Python 3.12+/3.13, pandas 2, NumPy 2,
scikit-learn >= 1.6; verified locally with pandas 3.1, NumPy 2.5, scikit-learn 1.9):

- `df.drop([...], 1)` -> `df.drop(columns=[...])` (positional axis removed in pandas 2)
- `np.mat` -> `np.asmatrix` (removed in NumPy 2.0)
- `float()` on a 1x1 matrix -> `as_float()` helper (NumPy 2.5 rejects it)
- `np.matrix` converted with `np.asarray` before it reaches scikit-learn (rejected since 1.8)
- `sklearn.cross_validation` -> `sklearn.model_selection`; `calinski_harabaz_score` -> `calinski_harabasz_score`
- `LogisticRegression(multi_class="ovr")` -> `OneVsRestClassifier(LogisticRegression())`
- `df.mean()` -> `df.mean(numeric_only=True)` (string columns no longer silently skipped)
- `SVM_Iris_Multiclass.py` resolves `../SVM_MNIST` relative to the file, not the cwd

`Algorithm/Adaboost/` is a byte-identical duplicate of `Algorithm/AdaBoost/`
(a case-only rename artifact); the manifest only lists `AdaBoost/`.
````

## 每個實驗該用什麼 Colab 設置
**全部用標準 CPU VM 就好。** 沒有任何一個實驗用 GPU 會變快：唯一的 PyTorch 腳本只訓練一層線性層，資料也只有幾百筆。所有實驗的 peak RSS 都低於 0.8 GB，也用不到 `--high-mem`。

| 批次 | 實驗 | 結果 | Session 時間 | CU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tier A | 23 個 sklearn / from-scratch 腳本 | 23/23 | 171 s | ~0.004 |
| Tier B | DecisionTree、FP-Growth、SVM_MNIST×2、CLiMF（皆 from scratch） | 5/5 | 25 min | ~0.034 |

- **費率**：實測 CPU VM 是 0.08 CU/h，和原本的估計一致。同樣約 28 分鐘換成 T4 大約 0.8 CU，A100 大約 5.6 CU，而且不會比較快。
- **速度**：Colab 只有 2 vCPU，跑純 Python 迴圈比本機慢 4–6 倍（例如 FP-Growth 本機 163 s，Colab 要 696 s）。所以只有在本機忙不過來時才值得丟上去。
- **還不能跑的**：Kaggle Elo（約 3 GB 資料，要 high-mem）、DCIC2019（比賽資料不在 repo）、`CLiMF_Epinions_TensorFlow.py`（要改寫成 TF2）。這些都照你選的先不處理，在 manifest 裡標成 `followup`，寫了缺什麼和建議的 runtime。HMM jieba/HanLP 需要 JDK，標成 optional，這次沒有跑。

## 改了什麼
- **舊程式相容性**：改了 25 個腳本，只修讓它在 pandas 2–3、NumPy 2.5、sklearn 1.9 能跑起來的地方，演算法和超參數都沒動。完整的修改清單在 `tools/colab/README.md`。
- **`pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`**：repo 裡其實沒有 `requirements.txt`，依賴是我從各腳本實際的 import 整理出來的。另外拆出 `torch`、`nlp`、`projects` 三個 extras。現在 `uv sync` 之後就能用 `uv run python Algorithm/...` 跑，README 也補了用法。
- **`tools/colab/`**：
  - `experiments.toml` 記錄每個實驗的資料、套件、runtime，以及在 Colab 實測的分鐘數。
  - `run_experiments.py --estimate` 會印出時間和 CU 的估算表；不加參數就上 Colab 跑，結束後在 `runs/colab/<時間>/out/report.md` 產生報告。
  - 在 VM 上 `plt.show()` 的圖會存到 `figures/`。
- `.gitignore` 加了 `.venv/` 和 `runs/`。
